title: Heuristic lower bounds on real Grothendieck constants of finite and infinite order
abstract: We propose candidate lower bounds on the real Grothendieck constants $K_{\mathrm G}(d)$ and their infinite-dimensional limit $K_{\mathrm G}$ using rotationally invariant cubic kernels. For the continuous construction, we identify an explicit threshold above which hemispherical binary strategies are unstable under cubic boundary deformations. Supported by numerical evidence, we conjecture that hemispherical strategies are globally optimal at this threshold. This conjecture would imply $K_{\mathrm G}\geq9π/16\simeq1.767146$, improving the rigorous lower bound $6π/11\simeq1.713596$. We also construct finite symmetric coefficient matrices from unit vectors in dimensions up to $24$. Large-scale see-saw optimization supports the continuous predictions and suggests improved lower bounds on $K_{\mathrm G}(d)$ in the studied dimensions from $4$ to $24$, conditional on the conjectured binary optima being exact. Selected matrices also yield finite-setting candidate dimension witnesses when interpreted as bipartite correlation Bell functionals. If the corresponding binary upper bounds hold, these witnesses would certify a local Hilbert-space dimension of at least five for each party.
summary: This theoretical paper derives improved heuristic lower bounds for the real Grothendieck constant, a quantity relevant to quantum information theory. The authors use a cubic kernel analysis to conjecture a new lower bound, significantly improving existing mathematical limits. The work also constructs specific matrices using high-dimensional lattices, linking abstract functional analysis to quantum correlation testing.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish heuristic lower bounds on the real Grothendieck constants, $K_G(d)$ and its infinite limit $K_G$. This constant is relevant to bounding the quantum-to-classical ratio in correlation Bell expressions.
main_result: The authors conjecture a new lower bound $K_G \geq 9\pi/16 \simeq 1.767146$ using a cubic kernel, which improves upon the previously known bound of $6\pi/11$.
method: The primary method involves analyzing the stability of 'hemispherical binary strategies' under cubic boundary deformations of rotationally invariant kernels, supplemented by large-scale optimization on finite dimensions using lattice constructions.
model_or_system: The mathematical framework involves optimizing ratios of quadratic forms defined by real matrices derived from unit vectors on the sphere, connecting functional analysis to quantum correlation bounds.
key_observables: The real Grothendieck constant $K_G(d)$ and its infinite limit $K_G$.
important_parameters: The cubic kernel parameter $c$, the critical parameter $c^*(d) = (d+1)(d+3) / (3(d+5))$, and the dimension $d$ (up to 24).
main_assumptions: The main conjecture is that hemispherical strategies are globally optimal at the critical threshold $c^*(d)$, and that the finite-setting lower bounds are exact.
paper_structure: The paper develops the problem by defining the Grothendieck constant using kernels, analyzes the continuous case using cubic deformations to find a conjectured bound, and then extends the results to finite dimensions using lattice-based matrix constructions.
why_interesting: The connection between bounding fundamental mathematical constants like $K_G$ and the structure of quantum correlations (Bell inequalities) provides deep theoretical insights into the limits of quantum information processing.
